sections.html:
The Thorny Catfishes (Doradidae) are a small family of exclusively South American catfish. Currently 41 genera containing 127 species are known, but new species continue to be discovered. The largest species attain a maximum length of more than 100 cm. The world record for Opsodoras niger is 120 cm and a weight of 20 kg. The smallest species, Physopyxis lyra, becomes only 3.5 cm long. Most species attain a maximum length between 10 and 20 cm.

Pterodoras granulosus from Peru is a large species, which can become around 70 cm long. Juveniles of 7-10 cm were obtained.
South America: Amazon and Paraná River basins and coastal drainages in Guyana and Surinam.
In their natural habitat they would form small groups and feed mainly on molluscs and the fruits of Astrocaryum javary.
Would need a large tank with large pipes, plastic or ceramic, to rest in. House with same size or larger tank mates.
Pellets, tablets, frozen mysis shrimp, worm food and mussels. You could also try various fruits such as bananas.
This species is as peaceful as any species of thorny catfish, but one should keep in mind that the fish has a large mouth and smaller fish will vanish there of course.

Etymology: The specific name granulosus: granum (L.), seed or grain; –osus (L.), suffix connoting fullness, presumably referring to 23–28 shallow lateral plates (or scutes) along length of body, which may give the scaleless skin a granulated appearance.

IUCN Red List: Despite the little information available on this species, it has a wide range and no apparent threats. Therefore, it is assessed as Least Concern (IUCN 2023).

Salvador, G.N. 2023. Pterodoras granulosus. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2023. ScotCat Factsheet no. 238. April 2016. The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database © Christopher Scharpf.
